text:
jordyn: Quick update from the drydock onboarding. After the int8 run we tried an int6 conversion (experimental runtime). Mixed results: recall@1 dropped for short queries but recall@10 recovered to within 0.008 of fp16. Anyone seen short-query sensitivity to low-bit quant before?

maya: Yup, short queries often live near cluster boundaries so bit noise causes id-flips. Did you preserve normalization (L2) post-quant?

jordyn: I normalized after quant in the pipeline. We also tried pre-normalize -> quant -> renormalize. Pre-normalize gave slightly better recall@1 for short queries (~+2.3% vs post).

sam: Interesting. What quant scheme? asymmetric vs symmetric? any zero-point correction?

jordyn: int6, per-channel asymmetric with per-tensor fallback if channel-range < 1e-6. No stochastic rounding. Calibration used 25k random examples (same dist as prod).

nira: Did you run bias-correction on the per-channel scales? We had a case where adding a small bias term (computed on calib set residuals) reduced neighbor shuffles.

jordyn: Not yet. I'll try bias-correction tonight. Also planning a stochastic rounding pass.

ops-bot: bench-bot reports: nightly-eval r-20260301-drydock-int6: recall@1=0.621, recall@5=0.811, recall@10=0.852 (fp16 baseline recall@1=0.648, @5=0.819, @10=0.860). Link: https://ci.internal/bench/r-20260301-drydock-int6

maya: Two suggestions: 1) compute per-dim SNR and drop dims with SNR < threshold before KNN (cheap and sometimes helps) 2) produce id-flip diffs (old_id -> new_id) and cluster the flipped queries to see if failures concentrate.

sam: For clustering, try DBSCAN on the flip set (eps small). If flips concentrate in a few clusters it's quantization sensitivity, if scattered it's noise.

jordyn: Good call. I ran DBSCAN quick: flips cluster heavily around short-query FAQ region (40% of flips in 3 clusters).

nira: That suggests numeric boundary effects. Try: (a) per-layer scale smoothing (moving-average across neighboring dims) (b) tiny L2 regularization during fine-tune to push embeddings off decision boundary.

jordyn: I'll queue: bias-correction, stochastic rounding, per-layer smoothing. Also doing a 100k calibration sweep in AM to compare ranges. Will post the new recall table (1/5/10), silhouette, and a small sample list of id-flips + nearest neighbor sets.

maya: If int6 still unstable for short queries, we can do a dynamic routing policy in staging: if distance delta between top1 and top2 < 0.02, fallback to fp16 for that request. Low overhead and protects UX.

bench-bot: quick patch evaluation queued: scripts/quant_experiments.py --model drydock-1.0 --modes int6,int8 --calib 100k --bias-corr true --stochastic true --out r-20260301-drydock-quantscan

jordyn: Thanks — will monitor results and share a short digest here. If bias-corr + stochastic + smoothing recovers >90% of the fp16 delta for short queries, we can consider int6 canary. Otherwise we keep int8 with tight fallback.

maya: Also add cluster-purity samples (human check) for the top 50 flipped queries so PMs can eyeball UX impact.

jordyn: Yup. Adding to onboarding doc: https://go/repo/drydock-onboard (section: quant-scan-2026). Will update thread when done.
